Additionally, TSA collects payment information from those members of the public whose claims are approved by TSA.  TSA estimates that approximately 1,250 claims are approved each year. provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

provenance.original: LE/FAMS applicants must self-certify certain information regarding their mental health, using the MHC form.  Based on its experience, TSA estimates that 100 applicants per year will be required to fill out the MHC form, which takes approximately 1 hour to complete.  This results in an annual hour burden of 100 hours (100 applicants x 1 hour).  Applicants can be any member of the public, therefore TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) all occupations (00-0000) mean wage rate of $32.66 per hour.  TSA then applies a load factor of 1.4582 to account for non-compensation costs of employment, such as health and retirement benefits.  This results in a fully loaded applicant compensation rate of $47.63.  TSA estimates an annual hour burden cost of $4,763.  Table 1 summarizes these calculations.
